newsitem.title: USA: GM's Saturn employees get $10,000 bonuses.
newsitem.headline: GM's Saturn employees get $10,000 bonuses.

text.p: Employees of General Motors Corp.'s Saturn unit will receive profit-sharing and incentive checks averaging $5,600 this week, bringing their total bonus for 1996 to $10,000, union officials Wednesday.
The payout marks the second year in a row that Saturn's 7,200 employees will receive the maximum $10,000 bonus award for hitting the company's profit, production, quality and training goals.
Dora Mack, a spokeswoman for United Auto Workers Local 1853 at Saturn's Spring Hill, Tenn., plant, said the hourly and salaried workers have already received $4,400 of the total bonus.

The Saturn bonus is the highest to be paid to workers by any U.S. automaker for 1996. The company does not have a traditional United Auto Workers contract, but instead operates with a Japanese-style "modern operating" agreement that emphasizes teamwork and employee initiatives.
Unionized workers at Saturn's parent, GM, will receive an average of only $300, down from $800 last year, because of GM's 18 percent drop in profits tor 1996.
Chrysler Corp is paying all of its workers an average 1996 profit-sharing payout of $7,900 in February, while Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday its workers will get an average of $1,800 in March.

Saturn does not disclose its financial results, but officials have said the unit was profitable on a fully accounted basis, which include amortization costs for GM's initial $5 billion Saturn investment.

Saturn production in 1996 reached a record 314,000 cars, up from about 301,539. The company did not lose any production in the model changeover for its redesigned coupe model, and it was able to recoup units lost during a GM brake plant strike in March 1996.
